newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude steady to higher, China buys Cabinda.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude steady to higher, China buys Cabinda.

text.p: Asian crude prices were steady to higher on Wednesday, with China showing a continued appetite for Cabinda crude.
The energy giant took three or four VLCCs of Cabinda for April loading, traders said.
China has now added 950,000 barrels of May 10-11 loading Cabinda to its tally. The seller was a French major.
Traders said the May Brent/Dubai has widened in recent weeks to $1.75 because of Dubai weakness after the IOC tender.
But the spread has started to narrow slightly again and was assessed Wednesday at a wide $1.45/$1.70, while June was assessed at $1.40/$1.50.
Traders said the freight rate has notched up slightly to Worldscale 62/65 from 60/62 over recent weeks, but the arbitage was open.
Most Middle East trading was coming to a close for May barrels, with mostly partials available to the market.
A separate French major was heard selling two partials of Murban and Umm Shaif to a U.S. major at ADNOC +2 cents and flat respectively.
However, traders said they heard a western trader sold a May Masila cargo at OSP +15 cents, the highest level to date for May loadings.
An Oman cargo was still available, traders said. It was peviously offered at MPM -5 cents, but there are no bidders, traders said.
On regional grades, a producer sold a top-up cargo of May Dulang crude at OSP +23 cents, matching the price level of a top-up Tapis done Friday to a Japanese trader.
May Belida was heard traded at ICP +40 cents, but no other details were mentioned.
